newsitem.title: UK: David S.Smith sees challenging conditions.
newsitem.headline: David S.Smith sees challenging conditions.

text.p: British packaging and paper maker David S. Smith will continue to fund trading conditions challenging until a sustained recovery takes hold in Europe, said chairman Alan Clements on Wednesday.

"This remains our view and as a result of a fiercely competitive trading environment, combined with the recent strength in sterling, we expect earnings in the second half to be lower than in the first half," he added.
The company announced pretax profits down 1.7 percent at 58.6 million in half year ended November 2, 1996.
"With the exception of the UK, there is no sense that the recovery in European markets is established or will be sustained and, as a result, market sentiment is poor," said the company.

In an outlook statement attached to the company's half year results it added "while the UK economy is experiencing good growth, the other major European economies are faring poorly with France among the worst. The recent strength of sterling in a fiercely competitive trading environment is unwelcome and is already weighing on the group's profitability."
